title: THE FIRST CONTACT
subtitle: A message from the unknown
opening: You are an ordinary person. Late one evening, an encrypted message appears on a device you rarely use. The sender claims to represent a confidential intelligence organization based in the Philippines. They know something about you—but they have not explained why they need your help.

lessons.title: Your First Instruction
lessons.explanation: print() sends information to the terminal. Text values are strings and must be wrapped in matching quotation marks. Python executes statements from top to bottom.

lessons.title: Multiple Signals
lessons.explanation: Each print() call normally ends its output with a newline. A comment begins with # and is ignored by Python; it exists to explain intent to people reading the code.
lessons.example:
# First status
print("SYSTEM ONLINE")
print("CHANNEL READY")

lessons.title: Operational Identity
lessons.explanation: A variable is a name bound to a value. Assignment uses =. A variable can be read later, allowing one value to be reused instead of repeating it.

lessons.title: Power Calibration
lessons.explanation: Integers represent whole numbers. Python supports +, -, *, /, //, and %. Use parentheses when you want to make calculation order explicit.

lessons.title: Repair the Shield
lessons.explanation: Stored values can participate in calculations. An assignment can replace the value currently associated with a variable.
lessons.example:
hp = 100
damage = 25
hp = hp - damage
print(hp)

lessons.title: Power Decision
lessons.explanation: A conditional chooses which indented block runs. The comparison energy > 0 produces True or False, so different inputs can lead to different outcomes.

lessons.title: Signal Sweep
lessons.explanation: A for loop repeats a block for each item in an iterable. range(1, 5) produces 1, 2, 3, and 4; the stop value is not included.

lessons.title: Threat Triage
lessons.explanation: A list stores multiple values in order. A loop can inspect each item, a condition can filter it, and a counter can record how many items match.
